record.paper_title: Recent results and open problems on parabolic equations with gradient nonlinearities
record.context_brief: Boundedness of global solutions in the intermediate q-range
record.original_question: For the semilinear parabolic problem u_t - Δu = |u|^{p-1}u - b|∇u|^q, what can be said about boundedness versus unboundedness of global-in-time solutions in the intermediate exponent regime 2p/(p+1) < q < p, excluding the already studied one-dimensional case q = 2? In particular, do all global solutions remain bounded, or can unbounded global solutions occur more generally in this range?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a smoothly bounded domain (or, when $n=1$, a bounded interval), and consider the semilinear parabolic problem with absorbing gradient term
$$
\begin{cases}
 u_t - \Delta u = |u|^{p-1}u - b\,|\nabla u|^q, & x \in \Omega,\ t > 0,\\
 u = 0, & x \in \partial\Omega,\ t > 0,\\
 u(\cdot,0) = \varphi, & x \in \Omega,
\end{cases}
$$
where $p > 1$, $b > 0$, and $q > 1$. A classical solution $u$ is called global if its maximal existence time satisfies $T^*(\varphi) = \infty$; it is called bounded if $\sup_{t \ge 0} \|u(t)\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)} < \infty$, and unbounded global otherwise.

It is known that in the one-dimensional case $\Omega = (0,L)$ with the special exponent $q = 2$ and $p > 2$, there exists $b = b_0(L) > 0$ and infinitely many initial data $\varphi$ producing nondecreasing-in-time, global, $L^\infty$-unbounded solutions.

Question. In the intermediate exponent range
$$
\frac{2p}{p+1} < q < p, \qquad q \neq 2,
$$
(in dimension $n \ge 1$, excluding the already-known case $q=2$ on an interval): must every global classical solution remain bounded, or can unbounded global solutions occur for some choice of $\Omega$, $b$, and $\varphi$? Provide a complete classification of boundedness versus unboundedness of global solutions in this regime.
artifact.category_tag: semilinear parabolic equations with gradient absorption
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface any work resolving boundedness versus unboundedness of global solutions for the equation $u_t-\Delta u=|u|^{p-1}u-b|\nabla u|^q$ in the intermediate range $2p/(p+1)<q<p$ with $q\neq 2$. Only the one-dimensional $q=2$ case appears to be settled (existence of unbounded global solutions). The general intermediate-$q$ question remains posed as an open problem in the recent survey literature.

status_evidence.snippet: Studies one-dimensional semilinear parabolic equation with gradient nonlinearity, addressing boundedness of global solutions in the case q=2.
status_evidence.claim: Only the one-dimensional q=2 case has been treated in detail; the intermediate range q≠2 remains open.
